title: Game- and Alcohol-Linked Atrial Fibrillation During the 2026 FIFA World Cup (GOAL-AF)
summary:
Acute cardiac arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter can be triggered or facilitated by short-term factors such as stress, alcohol consumption, sleep deprivation, or heat exposure. A study conducted during the 2006 FIFA World Cup already showed an increase in myocardial infarctions on days when the German national team played.

The GOAL-AF study investigates whether atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter occur more frequently during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, particularly after matches of the German national team, compared with a control period following the tournament. In addition, potential triggers such as alcohol consumption, stress, and sleep deprivation will be assessed. For this purpose, hospital routine data will be analyzed, and affected patients will additionally be surveyed using a brief questionnaire. The aim is to determine whether football matches and the associated stressors influence the occurrence of cardiac arrhythmias.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients who developed atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. In addition, a one-time questionnaire-based survey will be conducted to assess the occurrence of potential trigger factors associated with atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter
Control group - Retrospective analysis of all patients who developed atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter during a post–2026 FIFA World Cup control period.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Presentation to the emergency department
•	Documented or promptly objectively confirmed atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter
•	Sufficiently precise determination of the time of symptom onset
Exclusion criteria:
•	No objective documentation of atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter
•	Missing or non-usable information regarding the onset of the event
•	Atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter events likely related to a surgical procedure within the past 30 days
•	Atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter events occurring within 90 days after catheter ablation of atrial arrhythmias (blanking period)
•	Known permanent atrial fibrillation
